turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, Hale. My son found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I don't think this is productive.
Productive. You asked for this meeting, Hale, and you still haven't told me who decided on the zero or on what basis.
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.
Then you have ten minutes to tell me what you have besides a machine's score. If you walk out, I'm going straight to the principal's office and I'll want the reason for the zero in writing.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

I'm writing down that you said you're done here. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody contacted me. I'm going to the principal's office next, and the zero comes off before December 1.
